title: Counterfactual Probe Fabrication and Blame Prioritization Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a reproducible process for generating counterfactual probes (synthetic, minimally-perturbed inputs) and using them to prioritize blame signals during model regressions. The document ties together the probe factory (probe-factory service), the eval-orchestrator, and the triage-dashboard to create ranked hypotheses that accelerate root-cause identification and safe rollbacks.

Why this matters:
- Real production regressions often arise from subtle distribution shifts, tokenization changes, or quantization/kv-cache interactions.
- Counterfactual probes expose which axes of variation (prompt phrasing, context length, tokenization, quant-level) trigger delta behaviors.
- Systematic fabrication plus a principled blame prioritization rubric reduces MTTD/MTTR and avoids noisy rollbacks.

Scope and ownership:
- Scope: Applied-ML on-call and regression teams; covers model-serving regressions for hosted & dedicated deployments.
- In-scope artifacts: probe definitions, synthesized probe sets, blame scores, triage tickets, and replay bundles.
- Out of scope: aesthetic prompt edits for UX only, production rollout scheduling (handled by deployments team).
- Owners: Model regression squad (primary), Eval Platform (probe-factory integration), Serving Runtime (KV/quant telemetry).

Definitions and signals:
- Counterfactual probe: an input derived from a seed request by applying a controlled, minimal perturbation intended to reveal sensitivity to a single axis (e.g., tokenization boundary, punctuation variant, shortened context).
- Delta signature: hashed summary of model output change between baseline and candidate (e.g., intent flip, answer omission, hallucination marker).
- Blame score: numeric priority (0.0-1.0) estimating the likelihood that a subsystem change caused the regression.

High-level workflow (end-to-end):
1) Detection: alert from eval-sentinels or customer telemetry indicating a regression slice.
2) Seed capture: capture 50 representative seeds from the reported slice (live/probe stash).
3) Probe synthesis: feed seeds to probe-factory to create counterfactual families by axis.
4) Parallel evaluation: run probes in eval-orchestrator across candidate model artifacts (new model, previous model, quantized variants, cache-enabled vs cache-disabled).
5) Delta aggregation: compute delta signatures, create feature vector per axis.
6) Blame prioritization: apply metalogic (heuristic + learned combiner) to score subsystems.
7) Triage dashboard: surface top 3 hypotheses with repro steps and recommended mitigations.
8) Action: triage lead approves one of (rollback, hotfix patch, prompt adapt, config toggle).

Probe synthesis templates (examples):
- Axis: tokenization-boundary
  - Transform: insert zero-width space at subword boundary, alternative whitespace patterns.
  - Rationale: reveals tokenizer-dependent truncation or subword alignment bugs.
- Axis: context-trim
  - Transform: remove last n tokens (n in {8,32,128}) and re-evaluate.
  - Rationale: reveals kv-cache and attention fallback sensitivities.
- Axis: punctuation-orthography
  - Transform: swap hyphen vs en-dash, change curly quotes to straight, remove commas.
  - Rationale: surface fragile parsing/intent detection.

Example YAML probe bundle (for probe-factory ingestion):

---
bundle_id: cf-bundle-20250928-001
seeds: ["seed-1234", "seed-2237"]
axes:
  - name: tokenization-boundary
    params: {insert_positions: ["subword"], variants: ["zwsp"]}
  - name: quant-level
    params: {levels: [16, 8, 4]}
run_config:
  target_artifacts: ["model/v2.3.1", "model/v2.3.0-quant8", "model/v2.3.0-cacheoff"]
  parallelism: 32
  timeout: 600s
---

Evaluation matrix and requirements:
- The eval-orchestrator should run each probe-family across the target_artifacts and produce these outputs per run: output_text, logprobs, attention_cache_stats, tokenization_map, runtime_metrics (latency_ms, GPU_util).
- Minimum runs: 100 probes per axis for statistical confidence on noisy families.
- Acceptance SLO for probe latency scheduling: 95th percentile probe completion < 10 minutes for 100-probe families in normal load.

Blame scoring rubric (interpretable features):
- Signal alignment score (0-0.4): fraction of probes in an axis with matching delta signature versus control artifact.
- Artifact delta magnitude (0-0.3): aggregate semantic deviation weighted by slice importance (high-impact slices get more weight).
- Telemetry co-occurrence (0-0.2): correlation between runtime anomaly (e.g., cache evictions spike) and delta window.
- Historical priors (0-0.1): past frequency of regressions attributable to subsystem.

Blame score = sum of features (normalized to 0.0 - 1.0). Interpretation: >0.7 strong candidate; 0.4-0.7 medium; <0.4 low.

Sample blame table (text):
| Hypothesis | Blame score | Top contributing axis | Recommended immediate action | Confidence |
|-----------|-------------|------------------------|------------------------------|------------|
| KV cache regression due to missing prefix caching | 0.81 | context-trim | Toggle cache to "off" for slice; create rollback cluster | High |
| Quantization instability in layernorm | 0.56 | quant-level | Promote quant8->quant16 for experiments; schedule quant fix PR | Medium |
| Tokenizer update edge case | 0.38 | tokenization-boundary | Add tokenizer patch to canonicalizer; create probe to validate | Low |

Automated orchestration rules (default):
- If top hypothesis has score >= 0.75 and telemetry confidence is high, create a P0-rollback suggestion in triage-dashboard and queue a safety rollback candidate (requires SRE approval).
- If top hypothesis score between 0.5 and 0.75, open a labeled investigation ticket and schedule expanded probe run (increase probe count x3).
- If score < 0.5, mark as observation and continue monitoring; schedule human review if customer impact > 1% of queries.

Tracing and artifacts to attach for each triage ticket:
- bundle_id, probe manifest, per-probe JSONL (seed, transformed_input, target_artifact, output_text, logprobs).
- runtime traces from trace-collector: GPU_id, kernel_time_ms, kv-ejects, peak_mem_mb.
- diff report: delta_signatures.json (top-5 lexical diffs + semantic similarity score).

Rollout and canary guidance:
1) Shadow-run the suspect artifact with probes + 1% of live traffic for 24 hours before any rollback.
2) Canary step: if blame_score reduces below 0.3 for the artifact after config change, promote to 10% traffic.
3) Document change in release notes with "blame-hash" and probe-bundle reference.

Playbook runbook (operator steps):
1) Acknowledge alert and capture slice context in triage-dashboard.
2) Trigger probe-factory: select seed set + axes (use template "fast-triage-v1").
3) Monitor eval-orchestrator; if probe runs exceed 15 minutes per 100 probes, escalate to Eval Platform owner.
4) Review blame-ranked hypotheses; attach telemetry artifacts.
5) Decide action (rollback / config toggle / patch).
6) After action, run verification probe bundle and close ticket when delta signatures revert or customer impact is resolved.

Safety and privacy considerations:
- Probes made from customer data: enforce PII redaction using redact-agent before storage.
- Retention: probe artifacts retained 90 days by default, move to long-term archive only with privacy review.
- Access: only members of regression, eval-platform, and SRE roles can read probe results (RBAC enforced).

KPIs and SLAs to measure playbook effectiveness:
- Mean time to identification (MTTI) of root cause for high-impact regressions: target < 2 hours.
- True positive prioritization rate: fraction of top-1 hypotheses that lead to effective fix within 48h: target > 0.6.
- Probe-to-action latency (probe synthesis + eval): median < 25 minutes for fast-triage template.

Appendix A — Common CLI snippets:
- Create a probe bundle (probe-factory CLI):
  rwd-probe create --bundle cf-bundle-$(date +%Y%m%d)-$RANDOM --seeds-file seeds.json --axes tokenization-boundary,quant-level --targets model/v2.3.1,model/v2.3.0-quant8 --parallelism 32

- Fetch delta signatures:
  rwd-eval download --bundle cf-bundle-20250928-001 --artifact delta_signatures.json

Appendix B — Quick heuristics for axis selection:
- If regression started after infra deploy → prioritize runtime axes (kv-cache, gpu-kernel)
- If regression started after model change → prioritize model/artifact axes (quant-level, layernorm)
- If regression correlated with locale or punctuation → prioritize tokenization & orthography axes
